quizName: DMV Practice Test #9 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: A pre-ride inspection should:

options.text: Not be done before every ride.

questions.explanation: Check your motorcycle before every ride. It only takes a few minutes.

questions.question: It is a good idea to wear reflective clothing:
questions.explanation: Wear reflective and bright clothing anytime you ride. Crashes happen during the day and at night, so stay visible at all times.

questions.question: Where is the clutch lever usually located?
questions.explanation: The clutch lever is on the left handgrip.

questions.question: A motorcycle with a sidecar:

options.text: Can tip over if making a turn too fast.
Is designed to take corners at any speed.
Should not be used for loading items.

questions.correctAnswerText: Can tip over if making a turn too fast.
questions.explanation: A motorcycle with a sidecar can still tip over if you turn too sharply or go too fast around a corner.

questions.question: How do headache, cold, and hay fever medications usually affect your body?

options.text: They make you unable to concentrate.

questions.explanation: Most medications for headaches, colds, allergies, and hay fever make you drowsy and can impair your riding ability. Know how any medication affects you before riding.

questions.question: When riding a motorcycle, you should:

options.text: Not wear a jacket if it's warm out.
Always wear a jacket, even if it's warm out.
Not be concerned about long shoelaces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always wear a jacket, even if it's warm out.
questions.explanation: Always wear a long-sleeved jacket when riding, even in warm weather. It protects you and prevents dehydration. Also wear long pants and tuck in your shoelaces so they don't catch on the motorcycle.

questions.question: When riding behind a car, you should:

options.text: Ride in a position that will allow the other driver to see you in their rearview mirror.
Ride in the far left portion of the lane.
Ride in the far right portion of the lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in a position that will allow the other driver to see you in their rearview mirror.
questions.explanation: Position yourself so the driver ahead can see you in their rearview mirror. Ride in the center of the lane to be most visible.

questions.question: When it starts raining, it is usually best to:

options.text: Ride in the center of the lane.
Pull off to the side of the road until the rain stops.
Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the tire tracks left by cars.
questions.explanation: In wet conditions, ride in the tire tracks left by cars ahead of you. The left tire track is often best. Do not ride in the center of the lane.

questions.question: Which type of sign is yellow with black lettering or symbols?
questions.explanation: Warning signs are yellow with black lettering or symbols. They alert you to upcoming road conditions.

questions.question: Most motorcycle crashes happen:

options.text: After at least an hour of riding.
After more than 8 hours of riding.

questions.explanation: Most motorcycle crashes happen on trips shorter than five miles, within a few minutes of starting to ride.

questions.question: What does this hand signal mean when riding in a group?
questions.explanation: When the lead rider extends their left arm straight down with palm facing back, all riders in the group should stop.

questions.question: To control your motorcycle well, you should:

options.text: Use your arms to prop yourself up, not to steer.
Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance.
Let your feet hang off the footrests.
Sit far back so you have to stretch to reach the handgrips.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance.
questions.explanation: Keep your knees against the gas tank for balance in turns. Sit forward enough so your arms are slightly bent when holding the handgrips. Use your arms to steer, not to support yourself. Keep your feet firmly on the footrests.

questions.question: When carrying a passenger, a motorcyclist should tell the passenger to:

options.text: Sit as far back as possible.
Put their feet on the muffler.
Get on the motorcycle after the engine has been started.

questions.correctAnswerText: Get on the motorcycle after the engine has been started.
questions.explanation: Tell your passenger to get on only after you start the engine. Your passenger should sit as far forward as possible without crowding you and hold onto your waist, hips, or belt. They should keep both feet on the footrests at all times, even when stopped.

questions.question: Before mounting the motorcycle, your pre-ride inspection should include all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Check your tires, oil, fluids, lights, signals, clutch, throttle, mirrors, brakes, and horn before every ride. Do a thorough pre-ride inspection each time.

questions.question: How should your following distance at night compare to your following distance during the day?

options.text: Allow a longer following distance at night.
Allow a shorter following distance at night.
Always use the same following distance.

questions.correctAnswerText: Allow a longer following distance at night.
questions.explanation: At night, it's hard to judge distances because shadows and light are missing or distorted. Use a longer following distance at night than during the day.

questions.question: How often should a motorcycle operator check their mirrors?

options.text: More often than you look ahead

questions.explanation: Check your mirrors frequently to stay aware of hazards behind you.

questions.question: To avoid serious injury in a crash, you should do all of the following, except:
questions.explanation: Reduce injury risk by wearing an approved helmet, face or eye protection, and protective clothing.

questions.question: Which of the following best protects your eyes from wind?
questions.explanation: Goggles and face shields protect your eyes from wind. Most windshields, eyeglasses, and sunglasses do not.

questions.question: A rectangular sign may be a:
questions.explanation: Regulatory signs like speed limits are rectangular with white backgrounds and black lettering. Follow the rules posted on these signs.

questions.question: When riding at night:

options.text: Distances are easier to judge than during the day.
Using a high beam always makes it hard to see.

questions.explanation: At night, reduce your speed and increase your following distance. Use your high beam when there is no other traffic. Be ready to adjust your lane position as conditions change.

questions.question: What will protect your eyes from the wind?
questions.explanation: Goggles protect a rider's eyes from wind. Windshields, eyeglasses, and sunglasses do not provide enough protection.

questions.question: A person with a blood alcohol concentration (BAC) of ______ or higher is considered legally intoxicated.
questions.explanation: In Kentucky, a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher means you are legally intoxicated. Driving while intoxicated is illegal and dangerous.

questions.question: A proper lane position should do all of the following, except:

options.text: Increase your ability to see and be seen.
Communicate your intentions to other road users.

questions.explanation: A good lane position helps you see and be seen. It helps you avoid wind blasts, blind spots, and road hazards. It discourages other drivers from sharing your lane and gives you an escape route if danger occurs.

questions.question: If your motorcycle weaves over rain grooves or bridge gratings, you should:

options.text: Relax, maintain a steady speed, and ride straight across.
Tighten your grip on the handlebars and speed up to cross quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Relax, maintain a steady speed, and ride straight across.
questions.explanation: Weaving over rain grooves or bridge gratings is normal and not dangerous. Relax and ride straight across at a steady speed. Zigzagging is more dangerous than riding straight.

questions.question: How can you discourage another vehicle from sharing your lane?

options.text: Ride in the middle of your lane.
Ride in the left portion of your lane.
Ride in the right portion of your lane.
Swerve from side to side in your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the middle of your lane.
questions.explanation: Ride in the center of your lane to discourage other drivers from trying to share it.
